correctness.rationale: Propositions 1-2 verified: void probability and Slivnyak-Mecke give E[A]=1/lambda and the stated two-point integral with correct 1/(2pi) Jacobian from dv=2pi sinh r dr. Envelope 0<=J<=min implies e^{-max} majorant with integral 2, giving 0<=V<=1 and strict >0 on overlap set of positive measure. Lemma 3 verified: for fixed w_i>0 and theta!=0, d-(R1+R2)->log((1-cos theta)/2) finite, Fermi-coordinate box shows lens I uniformly bounded so J=lambda I->0 a.e.; DCT then gives M->1 and V->0, disproving any uniform a>0. Strict positivity plus V->0 also rigorously refutes strict decrease. Numeric V(1)=0.2566+-0.01 independently smoke-recomputed at coarse grid (M~1.2555, Eucl~1.2799) inside the wide interval; tail bound T(18)=6.09e-7 dominates exact 5.79e-7 and gaps in trio (0.2387/0.2566/0.2675) exceed ~3e-4 error budget by >30x.

No prior source states or implies the hyperbolic typical-cell area variance, the V(lambda)->0 low-intensity limit, the uniform-lower-bound impossibility, or V(1)~0.2566. Full-text check of the nearest ideal-tessellation paper confirms it treats convergence and first-order intensities, not second area moments. The hyperbolic lens DCT argument is not mechanically implied by Euclidean scaling.

The corrected picture 0<V<=1, V->0 at low intensity, V->V_eucl~0.280 at high intensity, with certified Var(area(C_1)) in [0.2466,0.2666], is a natural exact invariant of a pre-motivated object (Palm typical cell area) that was unknown, is not mechanically implied, and is retrievable for stochastic geometry. material_sources.title: Ideal Poisson–Voronoi tessellations on hyperbolic spaces - arXiv.org
material_sources.relationship_to_claim: Nearest prior on low-intensity hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi tessellations: proves distributional convergence of Vor(X_d(lambda)) to the ideal tessellation V_d, gives face intensities and expected k-volumes of typical faces, and describes the zero cell via a hemispherical deposition model with hole probability. Its hypotheses concern weak convergence of diagrams and first-order intensities; its conclusions state no second area moment, no scaled variance V(lambda), no V(lambda)->0 limit, and no numeric V(1) interval, so it does not imply the submitted variance disproof.

Its object class (hyperplane zero cell) and parameter regime differ from the submitted Palm typical Poisson-Voronoi cell area variance across lambda>0, so its exact formula cannot be specialized to V(lambda), V(lambda)->0, or V(1) in [0.2466,0.2666].
